title: A free freshness benchmark revalidates the pool's cited sources and reports the share of current, moved and source-dated lines and the time per question
goal: benchmarks.py run freshness (no model, no paid run) runs the lookup revalidation over the pool's answerable questions and records per provider host and over all: printed DOC lines current, moved, not found and source-dated only, wall time per question (median and p95) and requests made; the scenario's rows go to benchmarks.csv and its section to kb/_self/reports/benchmarks.md, with README.md's figures where the report summarises them; --dry-run prints the sources and requests it would make.

run: import csv, sys; sys.exit(0 if any(r.get('scenario') == 'freshness' for r in csv.DictReader(open('kb/_self/reports/benchmarks.csv', encoding='utf-8'))) else 1)

gates.question: Which pool rows does run freshness count as answerable, and how many does the recorded run use?
options: Rows of route good only; the recorded run uses --sample 5 (5 rows of each kind, seed 11), the default of run freshness being every such row
Rows of route good and split; the recorded run uses every row
Rows of route good only; the recorded run uses every row
gates.recommendation: Rows of route good only; the recorded run uses --sample 5 (5 rows of each kind, seed 11), the default of run freshness being every such row
gates.answer: Rows of route good only; the recorded run uses --sample 5 (5 rows of each kind, seed 11), the default of run freshness being every such row

gates.question: Under which provider host does a printed DOC line that cites several sources count, and what is a host's time per question?
options: The host of the source whose outcome the line prints (the worst of those it cites; its first source when none could be checked); a host's median and p95 are the wall times of the lookups that cite it
Every host the line cites counts it once; a host's time is the whole lookup's
gates.recommendation: The host of the source whose outcome the line prints (the worst of those it cites; its first source when none could be checked); a host's median and p95 are the wall times of the lookups that cite it
gates.answer: The host of the source whose outcome the line prints (the worst of those it cites; its first source when none could be checked); a host's median and p95 are the wall times of the lookups that cite it

notes: Planned 2026-10-12: benchmarks.py has no freshness scenario (benchmarks.py run freshness exits 2, unknown scenario) and PLANNED holds only pool, so a --dry-run of any other scenario starts it (BG-wapzksub): the worker adds freshness to PLANNED before the dry-run check can pass.
